newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea accepts Red Cross talks invitation.
newsitem.headline: North Korea accepts Red Cross talks invitation.

text.p: The North Korean Red Cross on Saturday accepted an offer by its Southern counterpart to reopen talks on speeding up food aid, the South Korean Red Cross said in a statement.

In a message relayed over a telephone "hotline" at the border village of Panmunjom, it agreed to meet next Friday, but insisted on Beijing as a venue. The Southern side on Friday had proposed a meeting in either Seoul, Pyongyang or Panmunjom.
Inter-Korean Red Cross talks were held for the first time in nearly five years on May 3 and 5 in the Chinese capital.

The South Korean Red Cross had called for those meetings to discuss sending food aid directly across the land border instead of by sea, or overland from China via the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
But the talks bogged down after North Korea said the South must first reveal the quantity of aid to be delivered before it would discuss delivery mechanisms.
In its invitation on Friday, the Southern side agreed to the North's demand.
